properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-31, supplying the architectural frame and three candidate patterns. Nothing chosen.

⭐ THE FRAME IS THE CONTRIBUTION, AND IT IS WORTH ADOPTING WHETHER OR NOT ANY PATTERN IS. His words: a graph-centric architecture is one where "a single, unified graph data structure serves as the primary source of truth and communication backbone" — common in compilers, game engines, CAD and system-modelling tools — and it is meant to be layered:

    BEHAVIOUR LAYER   modules that query, compute, and write results back
         ↓ queries / mutations
    DATA LAYER        pure nodes and edges; indexes, pointers, memory layout

His diagnosis: "BEHAVIOUR SMEARING" — the behaviour layer has collapsed into the data layer, so `DesignGraph` "is no longer just a graph, it has become the entire application".

⇒ WHY THAT FRAME EARNS ITS KEEP: it reclassifies the shared struct from DEFECT to KNOWN PATTERN WITH A KNOWN FAILURE MODE. reflow2 IS supposed to be graph-centric — that is what the product is. The question stops being "was the architecture wrong" and becomes "which layer did the behaviour end up in", which is answerable and repairable incrementally.

═══ HIS FOUR CONSEQUENCES, TESTED — see fact:change-fragility-is-crate-scoped-not-struct-scoped ═══
✅ Global coupling — confirmed: 45 of 88 modules, 62 impl blocks.
✅ Thread bottlenecks — confirmed, and measured INDEPENDENTLY hours earlier: one RwLock over the whole struct, concurrent export early in 91 of 200 trials.
🛑 Change fragility — TRUE BUT MISATTRIBUTED. All 88 core modules live in ONE crate, and the crate is Rust's compilation unit, so everything recompiles on any change regardless of the struct. Splitting the struct does not fix it; splitting the CRATE does. Two independent remedies for two different symptoms.
✅ Single source of truth / rich relationships — the advantages are real and are why the pattern was chosen.

═══ HIS THREE PATTERNS, SCORED AGAINST WHAT IS ALREADY DECIDED ═══
① VISITOR / QUERY DRIVERS — "an independent CircuitAnalyzer that takes a reference to the graph". ALREADY THE ESTABLISHED PATH HERE, applied three times as `pub fn granularity_report(g: &dyn GraphRead)` rather than as an analyzer struct. Same pattern, free-function flavour. Reach is 3 of 45. LOWEST RISK, PROVEN IN-TREE.
② ECS — strip properties into module-owned arrays. COLLIDES WITH A DELIBERATE DECISION: `create_node`'s contract says "the store is a property bag ON PURPOSE, so a design can record what reflow2 never anticipated". Typed per-module arrays need the property set known at compile time, which would remove the extensibility a USER's design depends on. A real option that trades away a product property, not an accident.
③ OPAQUE NODE HANDLES — `NodeId(42)`. The GOAL is right and the mechanism collides: reflow2's ids are semantic strings that are PUBLIC SURFACE, appearing in every tool call, the committed export, the skills and the prose. And the encapsulation he wants from it is already delivered by `GraphRead` without touching ids.
④ CRATE SPLIT — NOT ON HIS LIST, and it is the only one that addresses change fragility. It would also give the seam frontier something to measure: 56 of 64 uncovered coupling pairs cross no crate boundary today, which with two crates for 116 modules is arithmetic rather than a finding.

⚠️ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS. (1) Nothing has yet been BLOCKED by any of this — the case throughout is measurability and contention, not a defect anyone has hit. (2) Compile cost is asserted and never timed; `dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` suggests it has been FELT without being quantified, and the optimize skill would demand the number before the remedy. (3) `&dyn GraphRead` puts dynamic dispatch on the hottest read path and that cost is also unmeasured.

⭐ THE SEQUENCING THIS SUGGESTS, stated as an observation and not a plan: ① is incremental, reversible, proven, and each step buys a module its own measurability. ④ is the one with an unmeasured premise that could be measured cheaply first. ② and ③ each require overturning something already decided, so they want a decision rather than a migration.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2 is a graph-centric architecture that has smeared behaviour into its data layer; which decoupling does it take, and is a crate split on the list?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm discipline — ideas as ideas, nothing promoted, the collisions with existing decisions recorded beside the patterns rather than used to dismiss them.

The frame is kept separately from the patterns on purpose: adopting "graph-centric architecture with behaviour smearing" as the description costs nothing and improves how every later reader understands the shared struct, even if none of the four remedies is ever taken.
